# Problem

Consider a separable infinite-dimensional Banach space $B$ and a continuous linear injective map $f: E \rightarrow F$, where $E$ is a separable nuclear space and $F$ is a separable Banach space, both infinite-dimensional. Let $\otimes_{\epsilon}$ denote the injective tensor product of locally convex spaces (LCS) and $\hat{\otimes}_{\epsilon}$ its completion. Is the map $1_{B}\hat{\otimes}_{\epsilon} f: B\hat{\otimes}_{\epsilon} E \rightarrow B\hat{\otimes}_{\epsilon} F$ a continuous linear injective map?

$$1_B \hat\otimes_\epsilon f : B \hat\otimes_\epsilon E \to B \hat\otimes_\epsilon F$$

This is a known question about injective tensor products. The map $1_B \otimes_\epsilon f$ is always continuous linear. The question is injectivity.

This is because the injective tensor product respects subspaces: $\|z \otimes x\|_{Z \check\otimes X}$ can be computed via functionals on $X$, and Hahn–Banach extends functionals from the subspace $f(X)$ to $Y$ without increasing norm. So for Banach spaces, injective tensor product preserves injections of closed subspaces.
